sentences.text:
Sunita vs Abdul Samad Since Deceased By His Lrs on 6
October, 2025

Author: Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha
Bench: Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No. ______ Of 2025
 [@ Special Leave Petition (C) No. ______ Of 2025]

[@ Diary No. 1103 Of 2023]
 Sunita & Ors. 
 Versus
 Abdul Samad Since Deceased By His Lrs.& Anr. 
 O R D E R
1.

Heard Mr. Preetam Shah, learned counsel appearing for the appellants and Mr. Navneet Kumar and Mr.Parijot Kishore, learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
2. Delay condoned.
3. Leave granted.

4. This appeal arises out of the Judgment and order dated 07.01.2019 passed by the High Court of Karnataka, Bench at Kalaburagi in M.F.A.No. 32157 of 2013.
5.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka, Bench at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants are the wife, mother and children of the deceased.
They had filed a claim before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal [in short, the Tribunal] for a total compensation of Rs. 16 Lakhs.

6. By its order dated 09.07.2013, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs. 7,11,015/- with 6% interest against Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein and dismissed the case against Respondent No.3  Insurance Company.

7. By the impugned order dated 07.01.2019, the appeal filed by the appellants was allowed in part,
directing enhancement of compensation from Rs.7,11,015/- to Rs. 25,94,500/-.

The High Court Sunita vs Abdul Samad Since Deceased By His Lrs on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128115638/
1 observed that despite having been served, the respondents had failed to produce the Driving Licence and on the basis of this evidence, the Tribunal had come to the conclusion that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having a valid Licence and the Insurer has discharged its burden to prove the same.

entities.text: High Court Sunita vs Abdul Samad Since Deceased By His Lrs on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Tribunal, on Issue No. 2 as to whether the vehicle was driven with a valid licence or there was any violation of terms and conditions of the policy, had answered in favour of the Insurer and the Insurer was exonerated.

8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants has brought to our notice decision of this Court in Rama Bai Vs. Amit Minerals through Incharge Officer/ Competent Officer and Anr., reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 2067, the relevant portion of which is extracted below :-
5.

entities.text: Rama Bai Vs. Amit Minerals through Incharge Officer/ Competent Officer and Anr., reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 2067
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submission on part of the appellant that the High Court ought to have applied the pay and recover principle rests on the decision of this Court in Shamanna (supra) and Parminder Singh (supra).
In Shamanna (supra) this Court dealt with the claim of compensation by third party victim of the motor accident.

In para 5 of the judgment, this Court referred to its own earlier decision in National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Swaran Singh and Others to reiterate that the insurer has to pay the compensation amount payable to the third party and the insurance company may recover the same thereafter from the insured.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Swaran Singh and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.1 In Shamanna1 in which the doctrine of pay and recover was considered, the driver had no valid licence and the insurance policy was violated.

Similar principle, as applied in Parminder Singh2 in which the driver of the offending vehicle was found driving the vehicle in breach of the policy conditions, the insurance company was absolved and the principle of pay and recover was applied.

5.2 It was pointed out on behalf of respondent No. 3 - Insurance Company that in subsequent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v. Parvathneni and Another5 , this Court doubted the justification of applying the principle of pay and recover on the ground that if the Insurance Company was found not liable in law to pay the compensation, the direction regarding pay and recover can be said to be beyond the legal propriety.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Parvathneni and Another5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5.2.1 In the earlier decisions in National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Yellamma, Samundra Devi v. Narendra Kaur, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Brij Mohan8 and New India Insurance Co. v. Darshana Devi this Court had applied the very principle, about the correctness of which, reservations were expressed in Parvathneni.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Yellamma, Samundra Devi v. Narendra Kaur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Brij Mohan8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: New India Insurance Co. v. Darshana Devi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.2.2 However, as found in Shamanna1 the reference was not answered and the case was disposed of on 17.09.2013, keeping the question of law open to be decided in an appropriate case.
6. In the present case as stated above, on the date of accident, the driver had no valid license and the licence was not renewed.

The insurance company was entitled to take a valid defence in that regard under Section 149 (2)(a)(ii) as the driver of the Sunita vs Abdul Samad Since Deceased By His Lrs on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128115638/
2 offending vehicle was not duly licensed, to avoid its liability to pay the compensation.

entities.text: Sunita vs Abdul Samad Since Deceased By His Lrs
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The conditions in law are satisfied to absolve the insurance company from the payment of compensation.

6.1 The High Court in the impugned judgment relied upon the decision in Ram Babu Tiwari to find that as per the specific provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, if the driver does not possess a valid and effective driving licence,
it results in a breach of conditions of the insurance policy, exonerating the insurer from its liability.

But while affirming the order of the High Court, absolving the liability for breach of conditions in the policy, this Court refused to interfere with orders of pay and recover as directed by the High Court.

7. In the above circumstances, going by the series of decisions of this Court, it is only proper that the insurer be directed to satisfy the award, which however can be recovered by the insurer from the insured-owner of the vehicle.
The appeal stands allowed.

9. In view of the fact that the principle of pay and recover was adopted even in case of no valid licence, we are of the opinion that the said principle can be applied in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
10. In this view of the matter, we allow the appeal and direct Respondent No. 3  Insurance Company to pay compensation to the claimant(s) and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
The amount shall be paid within a period of three months from today.
.J. [PAMIDIGHANTAM SRI NARASIMHA]
... J. [ATUL S. CHANDURKAR] NEW DELHI;
OCTOBER 06 2025.
